feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: The latest health and science news. Updates on medicine, healthy living, nutrition, drugs, diet, and advances in science and technology. Subscribe to the Health & Science podcast.

entry.title: Researchers are tracking Monarch butterflies to learn more about their journey
entry.summary: Researchers all over North America are attaching tiny transmitters to Monarch butterflies as they begin their migration to Mexico, to learn more about their stops and challenges.

entry.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
entry.summary: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.

entry.title: The origin of the chew: When did we learn to eat like this?
entry.summary: It's likely you've already chewed and swallowed some tasty morsel today. But when did that ability emerge? New evidence points to at least the middle Jurassic, back when dinosaurs still reigned.

entry.title: Isaias pummels the Gulf Coast, and plows through Alabama
entry.summary: Hurricane Isaias landed Friday night on the Florida Gulf Coast. The storm was expected to bring life-threatening storm surge, damaging winds, flooding and the possibility of tornados.

entry.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software sent humans to the moon, dies at 90
entry.summary: Hamilton was in her early thirties when she led the team of software engineers that powered NASA's Apollo missions. She later said, "There was no choice but to be pioneers."

entry.title: Study finds 194-year-old tortoise is 'aging more slowly than you would expect'
entry.summary: Researchers are studying the genome of the world's oldest land animal — a 194-year-old tortoise named Jonathan — to uncover secrets about his longevity.

entry.title: 4 people on NASA's Crew-12 mission return to Earth after 8 months in space
entry.summary: Four people — two NASA astronauts, one from the European Space Agency and a Russian cosmonaut — spent nearly eight months at the space station, conducting spacewalks, science experiments and research.

entry.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
entry.summary: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

entry.title: How 'Musk' director Alex Gibney became a critic
entry.summary: A trove of documents and interviews with people close to tech billionaire Elon Musk reveal a damning picture of his rise as one of the world's richest and most powerful men.
